etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English misleden, from Old English mislǣdan (“to mislead”), from Proto-Germanic *missalaidijaną (“to mislead”), equivalent to mis- +‎ lead.

definitions.definition: (literally) To lead astray, in a false direction.

quote.citation: 2004, Green Day (lyrics and music), “Jesus of Suburbia”, in American Idiot:
quote.text: City of the dead / At the end of another lost highway / Signs misleading to nowhere

definitions.definition: To deceive by telling lies or otherwise giving a false impression.
To deceptively trick into something wrong.
A wrong or bad lead; a leading in the wrong direction.

quote.citation: 1951, Improvement of Grading Practices for the Air Training, page 31:
quote.text: If all the misleads (incorrect alternatives) are illogical, absurd, or in any way unattractive as possible answers, the student has no difficulty in choosing the correct answer.

definitions.definition: (countable) That which is deceptive or untruthful (e.g. a falsehood, deception, untruth, or ruse).

quote.text: The skinny body, a mislead to make people think that he was captured by someone and tortured. Even the loud gunshot was a mislead to make them ask questions to common citizens. His long untidy hair, also a mislead.
